statement: Using the Frobenius Alexander quandle convention and the quandle-isomorphism/Frobenius-similarity equivalence of arXiv:2609.02278v1, the least rational prime ell != 5 such that, uniformly for all elliptic curves A,B over F_5, isomorphic quandles Q(A[ell],pi_A,ell) and Q(B[ell],pi_B,ell) force A and B to be F_5-isogenous is ell=11. Uniform sufficiency holds at 11. The smaller eligible primes all fail: at ell=2 use y^2=x^3+3x and y^2=x^3+1; at ell=3 use y^2=x^3+3x+2 and y^2=x^3+4x; at ell=7 use y^2=x^3+3x and y^2=x^3+4x+2. In each pair the curves are nonsingular and nonisogenous, while their torsion Frobenius operators have the same explicitly certified rational canonical form.
contribution: This supplies a complete proof of the frozen least-prime problem. It exactly settles the finite ell=2,7 delta left by the inspected primary source, independently rechecks its ell=3 example with full certificates, and combines these failures with the sharp trace-diameter proof at ell=11. The literature screen is bounded and no absolute priority claim is made.
